ACCPPDE101.name: Personal & Professional Development
ACCPPDE101.finding: Mandatory first-year academic writing, source evaluation, reflective inquiry and civic collaboration.

BENECON111.name: Introduction to Economics
BENECON111.finding: Economic models of markets and policy supply foundations for the trial’s public-economics analysis; not a Slavic regional economy course.

BENECON311.name: Public Economics
BENECON311.finding: Welfare, health, education, insurance, taxation and redistribution provide a substantive social-model bridge, without a documented Slavic regional comparative welfare sequence.

BENGATE102.name: Research Methods & Statistics
BENGATE102.finding: Empirical design, surveys, measurement, inference and a full data-collection project supply social-research methods; no Slavic regional field setting is prescribed.

GOSGATE102.name: Law, Society & Justice
GOSGATE102.finding: Socio-legal analysis of institutions, rights, justice and social control supplies a complementary institutional method; not Slavic legal study.

GOSHIST111.name: Modern History
GOSHIST111.finding: Modernity, revolution, nationalism, imperialism, world wars, Cold War and the fall of communism give real historical foundations. Current evidence supports broad modern history, without the older specific Russian-Revolution claim or a sustained Eastern European course sequence.

GOSHIST112.name: Histories of Gender
GOSHIST112.finding: Gender, family, sexuality, memory, interviews and cultural representation provide concrete historical methods and themes; the documented setting is North America.

GOSHIST211.name: History of Empires
GOSHIST211.finding: Comparative imperial power, ideology, administration and cultural legacies support historical explanation; specific Slavic regional colonial histories are not established.

GOSHIST311.name: Native American Histories
GOSHIST311.finding: Indigenous histories, institutional violence, resurgence and relational collaboration provide a real methodological connection to Indigenous cultural inquiry; Native American teaching is not regional minority regional instruction.

GOSHIST312.name: Researching the “American Century”
GOSHIST312.finding: The current official description supports historical questions, source criticism, interdisciplinary methods and a substantial paper. Its American title and bounded content do not establish Slavic regional research. The excluded historical outline is not used.

GOSLAWJ111.name: Human Rights: Law & Philosophy
GOSLAWJ111.finding: Rights institutions and philosophical claims support questions of minorities, identity and recognition; not specifically Slavic regional rights history.

GOSLAWJ212.name: Introduction to Public International Law
GOSLAWJ212.finding: International law, self-determination, rights, institutions and postcolonial perspectives support cross-border and colonial comparison; not an regional legal sequence.

GOSLAWJ213.name: Comparative Constitutional Law
GOSLAWJ213.finding: Comparative constitutional institutions, rights and case interpretation offer concrete tools for political comparison, without establishing Slavic institutional study.

GOSLAWJ312.name: Foundations of European Union Law
GOSLAWJ312.finding: EU institutions, citizenship, free movement and casework provide relevant European connections, without a Slavic regional institutional/cultural focus.

GOSPHIL212.name: Ethics
GOSPHIL212.finding: Ethical theories and independent normative argument illuminate values, practices and meaning; not the region’s intellectual history.

GOSPHIL311.name: Philosophy of Emotion
GOSPHIL311.finding: Theories of emotion, art, politics and lived experience provide concepts for cultural interpretation; no Slavic regional case sequence is specified.

GOSPOLI111.name: Introduction to Political Philosophy
GOSPOLI111.finding: Political authority, rights and ideological traditions support analysis of social models; no sustained Slavic regional intellectual or political history is established.

GOSPOLI112.name: Foundations of Comparative Politics
GOSPOLI112.finding: Empirical comparison of democracy, institutions, behaviour and autocratisation gives substantial comparative-political methods. A possible region-focused research choice is not a guaranteed Eastern European taught sequence.

GOSPOLI212.name: Theory of International Relations
GOSPOLI212.finding: IR theories, cases and a researched UN simulation offer international institutional inquiry; a possible Slavic regional country choice cannot establish taught regional depth.

GOSPOLI311.name: European Union Politics
GOSPOLI311.finding: EU institutions, integration and an empirical parliamentary-amendment project offer substantive European political methods; not a Slavic politics sequence.

GOSPOLI312.name: Public Policy Analysis
GOSPOLI312.finding: The description supports globalisation, policy processes, a sugar case and policy memos; this receives full weight without inventing Slavic regional policy cases.

GOSPOLI313.name: Peace & Conflict
GOSPOLI313.finding: Conflict, colonial legacies, identity, rights and peacebuilding provide interdisciplinary comparison, not documented Baltic/regional regional study.

GOSSOCI111.name: Introduction to Sociology
GOSSOCI111.finding: Solidarity, modernity, identity, inequality and social boundaries supply direct social concepts, with general applications rather than a Slavic survey.

GOSSOCI212.name: Qualitative Research Methodology
GOSSOCI212.finding: Interviews, observation, ethnography, coding and reflexive research support regional-study methods; a freely chosen Slavic regional project is not guaranteed instruction or supervision.

GOSSOCI214.name: Modern Sociology
GOSSOCI214.finding: Modernity, coloniality, identity and social theories support comparative social interpretation; their documented scope is broader than Slavic regional societies.

GOSSOCI215.name: Social Movements & Environmental Justice
GOSSOCI215.finding: The description establishes social movements and environmental justice through feminist, anticolonial and other perspectives. These can frame land/identity issues without establishing regional/regional minority teaching.

GOSSOCI311.name: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory
GOSSOCI311.finding: Civil society, solidarity, trust, public spheres and research on organisations support social-system questions, without a documented Slavic regional welfare/civil-society sequence.

HCBBIOM111.name: Epidemiology & Public Health
HCBBIOM111.finding: Health determinants, causal study designs, needs assessment and population evidence support social-system comparison; no Slavic regional health-system case is established.

HCBCOGN312.name: Psycholinguistics
HCBCOGN312.finding: The description substantively teaches language processing, acquisition, bilingualism, semantics, speech, reading and experimental approaches. It is a genuine language-science contribution, but not Slavic sociolinguistics or mutual intelligibility.

HCBGATE102.name: Introduction to Brain & Behavior
HCBGATE102.finding: Brain/behaviour concepts and psychological/neuroscientific methods prepare for psycholinguistics; the remaining clinical/behavioural material cannot be treated as regional cultural study.

MCCCOMM111.name: The Art of Rhetorical Communication
MCCCOMM111.finding: Rhetorical analysis, argument, discourse and storytelling provide concrete textual/communicative tools, not Slavic language competence.

MCCCOMM211.name: Style & Meaning
MCCCOMM211.finding: Stylistics connects grammar, discourse and cognition to literary/nonfiction interpretation. This is substantive linguistic analysis, without a Slavic linguistic/source-language sequence.

MCCCOMM311.name: Persuasive Communication
MCCCOMM311.finding: Persuasion, framing and research-based community communication provide applied discourse methods; its sustainability projects do not establish Slavic regional communication study.

MCCCOMM312.name: Creative Communication Laboratory
MCCCOMM312.finding: Poetry, performance and scholarship-grounded creative practice provide a complementary way to explore language, voice and embodiment, not Slavic regional source-language or translation training.

MCCHEAM111.name: Introduction to Western Art History
MCCHEAM111.finding: Western painting and contextual visual research support cultural-history interpretation, without evidence of a Slavic regional art-historical focus.

MCCHEAM211.name: African Art & Heritage
MCCHEAM211.finding: African visual traditions, colonial collecting and restitution provide actual material-culture and heritage inquiry; they are not Slavic cultural history.

MCCHEAM316.name: Writing Art's Histories
MCCHEAM316.finding: The description supports art historiography, interpretation, authorship/identity and global disciplinary critique. These methods receive full consideration without invented regional examples.

MCCLITR111.name: Introduction to Literary Studies
MCCLITR111.finding: Close reading, genre, narrative, symbolism and critical-source use directly support literary interpretation as a method; no region-specific corpus is established.

MCCLITR112.name: Great Literary Works
MCCLITR112.finding: Ancient-to-modern literary comparison, historical context and textual analysis support comparative literary history, without a sustained Slavic regional corpus.

MCCLITR211.name: World Myth & Literature
MCCLITR211.finding: Comparative myth and narrative theory, including Norse material in the official description, provide real comparative literary methods. Norse is not Slavic, and the documented teaching does not establish a Slavic myth/literary-history sequence.

MCCLITR212.name: Life & Travel Writing
MCCLITR212.finding: Life/travel writing, memory, identity and cultural positioning provide direct methods for narratives of place and belonging; no Slavic regional travel/memory corpus is established.

MCCLITR311.name: Film & Text
MCCLITR311.finding: Adaptation, intertextuality and close literary/film research support text-image and reception inquiry, without an established Slavic regional regional focus.

MCCLITR312.name: Perspectives on Literary Meaning
MCCLITR312.finding: The description establishes humanist, feminist, Marxist, minority and psychoanalytic interpretation with a research project. These methods do not themselves provide Slavic texts or contexts.

MCCMEDI111.name: Introduction to Film & Media
MCCMEDI111.finding: Film form, history, representation and feminist/postcolonial interpretation provide media-analysis methods, without a Slavic regional drama/film sequence.

MCCMEDI112.name: Media Archaeology
MCCMEDI112.finding: Media materiality, technologies, communication and memory provide historical-cultural inquiry; Slavic urban/digital-language research is not established.

MCCMEDI211.name: From T.V. to TikTok
MCCMEDI211.finding: American media, identity, Indigenous self-representation and speculative futures supply specific cultural comparison, not Slavic regional popular culture.

MCCMEDI311.name: Media & Race
MCCMEDI311.finding: Racial construction, exclusion, media and observation/archive/podcast methods support identity research; the American setting is not converted into Slavic minority history.

MCCMEDI312.name: The Documentary
MCCMEDI312.finding: Documentary history explicitly includes Soviet filmmaking, propaganda, advocacy, ethnography and historical representation, plus film-production research. This is an actual regional cultural bridge; the broader sequence does not establish sustained Eastern European cinema, literary history or contemporary society.

candidates.concept: Slavic language, linguistics and language-mediated culture
candidates.assessment: A full trial combines psycholinguistics, stylistic/grammatical analysis, literature, rhetoric, media, historical and qualitative/social methods. This supplies substantial language-and-culture inquiry but not Slavic historical morphology, aspect, source-language literature and region-specific cultural research. Missing language acquisition alone is not the no-match criterion.

candidates.concept: Eastern European literature, cultural history and intellectual life
candidates.assessment: A full trial tests the complete literature sequence, life writing, adaptation, cultural theory, art/heritage, film/documentary and historical research. Soviet documentary cinema is a genuine regional connection and is not ignored. It does not extend into sustained Russian, Polish, Czech or Balkan literary, intellectual and cultural history; the larger programme becomes general cultural humanities.

candidates.concept: Russian and Eastern European history, politics, society and conflict
candidates.assessment: A full trial tests modern and imperial history, European institutions, comparative politics, international relations, conflict, sociology, qualitative inquiry and public policy/economics. These offer concrete analysis of institutions, power and change. They do not accumulate into sustained study of Eastern European histories, post-Soviet societies, Balkan conflicts or region-specific sources; the resulting programme becomes broader European/global social science.

academicChallenge: Language/culture trial gives genuine psycholinguistic experimental and stylistic linguistic analysis, literary interpretation and qualitative research. Cultural-history trial tests all literature, film/text, art/heritage, documentary and historical methods; Soviet documentary is a genuine bridge. Social/political trial tests European institutions, conflict, modern/imperial history, sociology and concrete public-policy/economic methods. These are coherent general fields but their combined subject matter does not sustain Slavic regional inquiry. Neither a disciplinary-equivalence quota nor language absence alone determines the result. Description-only psycholinguistics, literary meaning, historiography, current American Century research, policy and social movements receive full supported consideration.
progression: All three trials are complete and feasible. Brain/Behaviour precedes Psycholinguistics in its sole 2027h1 planned slot. Literary, media and social foundations precede advanced work where possible. Economics and methods precede Public Economics. No offering was restored. GOSHIST312 uses only current American Century description; excluded Walcheren outline is not used.
